title: Observation-only: terminal-capacity saturation is workload-mix intrinsic; no query_execution knob is causally implicated by the verified incumbent
configuration_cause: None identified in the query_execution knob set. The incumbent already routes every access through an index (idx_scan 23774/s, seq_scan 0.0/s), serves 99.992% of buffer accesses from shared memory (buffer_hit_ratio 0.9999213, blks_read 23.31/s vs blks_hit 296142/s, blks_hit_per_txn 9.28), and selects an actual Index Scan for the sampled point lookup (estimated_rows 1.0, estimated_total_cost 8.45, far below any jit_above_cost threshold, so jit=on cannot be firing). The reported saturation is a property of the closed-loop transaction mix (GetUserTweets = 3449949 of ~3.83M client transactions, ~90%) that consumes 843.5s of the 960s finite terminal budget, not a consequence of a mis-set planner/executor knob.
mechanism: Closed-loop control: goodput_rps = terminals / weighted-mean client latency. Observed 8 terminals / 249us = 32.1k rps, matching the measured 31.9k rps. The weighted mean is dominated by GetUserTweets (mean 244.5us, p50 157us, p99 2280us, 90% of calls), so the entire terminal budget is one class of cache-resident index lookups. Two structural facts bound what any query_execution knob can do: (1) GetUserTweets is read-only, so it never enqueues on the WAL commit path - wal_write (229.0/s) exactly matches InsertTweet count (38387 in 168.4s = 228.4/s) and wal_bytes_per_txn is 4.77B, i.e. the wal_wait alert is carried by a single sampled waiter (wal_waiting_backends median 0, p95 0, max 1) with 0.134ms average WAL write latency and zero host I/O stall; (2) GetUserTweets adds no physical I/O to remove (9.28 buffer hits/txn, 0.00073 physical reads/txn). What remains is executor/lock-manager micro-stall in the tail (mean 244.5us vs p50 157us, i.e. ~87us of mean is tail), which no allowed knob (jit, random/seq_page_cost, effective_*_size, *_collapse_limit, parallel settings, work_mem, temp_buffers) addresses for a cached single-index path, and which is inside the +-3.5% replicate spread (verified replicates 29762.6 / 30213.6 / 31906.7 rps; GetUserTweets p50 165/169/157us).
query_effect: No query, plan or access path is changed. The diagnosed statement class (GetUserTweets) already executes as a cached index access path; the sampled plan evidence (Index Scan, cost 8.45, rows 1.0) confirms index usage and no JIT eligibility. The only measurement gap is that the sampled EXPLAIN is for a different statement (SELECT * FROM tweets WHERE id=1) than the budget-dominating class, so no plan mutation is justified on this evidence.
expected_tps_effect: unchanged: no knob is changed; the incumbent sits at 29762.6-31906.7 rps (median 30213.6) and is expected to remain inside that replicate band.
expected_latency_effect: unchanged: GetUserTweets p50 ~157us / p99 ~2280us keeps consuming ~0.88 of terminal capacity; the non-dominant classes stay at their measured shares (GetFollowers 0.0514, GetTweetsFromFollowing 0.0367, InsertTweet 0.0223, GetTweet 0.0070).

predictions.rationale: Closed loop identity 8 terminals / 249us mean = 32.1k rps reproduces the measured 31.9k rps; with no change we predict throughput stays within +-5% of the incumbent band 29762.6-31906.7 rps.

p50 157us is a shared-memory index access (buffer_hit_ratio 0.9999213, blks_read_per_txn 0.00073); no allowed knob changes the executor path for this plan. Baseline p50s were 165/169/157us (+-4%), so a 10% tolerance bound is conservative.

p99 2280us (baselines 2451/2486/2280us) is executor/lock-manager micro-stall on hot cached pages; the query_execution knob set contains no lever for that path, so we predict no movement beyond the observed replicate spread.
0.8787 = 843.5s / (8 terminals * 120s); baselines were 0.8798/0.8817/0.8787. Count and mean latency are both unchanged by a no-op, so the fraction stays ~0.88 within +-5%.

Measured 0.1345ms average per WAL write with host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0; the wal_wait alert rests on a single sample (wal_waiting_backends median 0, p95 0, max 1). A genuine WAL-stall mechanism would require an order-of-magnitude higher write latency or sustained waiters, so we predict the mean stays within +-0.5ms.

alternatives.statement: The GetUserTweets tail (p99 2280us, max 27247us) is a WAL commit/fdatasync stall propagated from InsertTweet commits under wal_sync_method=open_datasync and wal_writer_delay=215ms, matching the high-severity wal_wait alert.

The finite terminal budget is consumed by client-side result handling and protocol round trips rather than server execution, as suggested by client_waiting_backends p95=5 of 8 connections and idle_in_transaction p95=3.
The tail comes from physical reads because shared_buffers (53504 pages ~ 437MB) cannot hold the hot set on this 2.16TB host.

cross_domain_requirements: query_execution measurement gap: no EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) exists for the exact GetUserTweets statement, only for SELECT * FROM tweets WHERE id=1 (Index Scan, cost 8.45); plan-level claims about that class must not be made until it is captured.
concurrency_maintenance: confirm commit_delay=671us with commit_siblings=12 is inert at the observed 9-10 backends (guard can never be satisfied), i.e. it cannot be the source of either alert.

memory_storage: if a future round needs more read-path margin, shared_buffers=53504 pages and huge_pages=off are the restart-class levers; current evidence (0.9999213 hit ratio) does not justify them.
why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not, and this proposal deliberately claims no improvement: knob_changes is empty because the two diagnostic alerts are structural or unsupported by the incumbent's own evidence. client_terminal_saturation is an algebraic consequence of a fixed 90%-dominant transaction class over cached index lookups, and wal_wait is carried by wal_waiting_backends max=1 against 0.1345ms average WAL write latency and zero host I/O stall, while 100% of WAL writes coincide with InsertTweet (229.0/s vs 228.4/s) and GetUserTweets is read-only. Any change inside the allowed query_execution set is bounded by the 87.9% share of a path that has no physical I/O and no spill to remove, i.e. below the +-3.5% replicate noise; proposing one would be an unevidenced gamble. The correct next action is measurement-only: capture EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) and per-wait-event timing for the exact GetUserTweets SQL before any knob is touched.
